topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: L1-L3 Caches
explanation: The memory hierarchy mitigates the latency gap between the CPU and main memory (DRAM) by employing multiple levels of high-speed static RAM (SRAM) caches. These levels, typically L1, L2, and L3, are characterized by increasing capacity and decreasing proximity to the CPU core, resulting in higher latency. L1 is the fastest and smallest, often split into instruction and data caches. Effective caching relies on the principle of locality of reference (temporal and spatial), ensuring frequently accessed data is retained in the faster cache levels, thereby minimizing costly main memory access cycles and maximizing instruction throughput.
